rationale: Rev 11:8 directly applies the spiritual name Egypt to the great city identified by the clause 'where also our Lord was crucified,' which is Jerusalem. Gal 4:25 independently states that the present Jerusalem 'is in bondage with her children,' while Isa 1:10 already addresses Jerusalem's rulers as Sodom and Matt 23:37 / Rev 18:24 fix the blood of the prophets on the same city. These texts together establish the entry's identification more tightly and with fewer extra-textual steps than the generic bondage/world reading, which must treat the crucifixion clause as non-locative or merely illustrative. Secondary descriptors in the entry (covenant city, worldly rule, covenant corruption) follow directly from the same verses once the referent is fixed. No material assertion printed in the entry lacks support; broader chapter claims (Babylon identity, rod-serpent arc, western geography) lie outside glossary scope.
book_core_identification: The spiritual name Egypt in Revelation designates Jerusalem—the covenant city that is in bondage and corruption—as the great city where the Lord was crucified.
book_secondary_elaborations: A covenant city in bondage under worldly rule
Jerusalem in bondage and covenant corruption
chapter_only_objections: Full equation of Babylon the Great / the harlot with Jerusalem via Aaron's rod becoming the serpent and riding the beast
Geographic claim that the last Babylon is the westernmost bloc of seven mountains
Extended Exodus-plague and millstone-sinking typology applied scene-for-scene to the fall of Babylon
Identification of the tail as the lying prophet and the almond rod as restored priesthood
strongest_counter_interpretation: Egypt functions throughout Scripture as the standing symbol of bondage to sin and the oppressive world-system; Rev 11:8 simply applies that established symbol (together with Sodom) to whatever great city is in view, without redefining the term Egypt itself as Jerusalem.
counter_core_identification: Egypt symbolizes bondage/slavery to sin and the godless world-system from which God delivers his people.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the spiritual name Egypt has Jerusalem (the covenant city in bondage) as its referent; it treats Egypt as a transferable quality or type rather than the name of that specific city.
counter_case: Exodus 1–15, Deut 5:6 and the repeated 'house of bondage' formula establish Egypt as the paradigmatic domain of slavery independent of any later city
1 Cor 10:1–11 and Heb 11:24–27 treat the Exodus events as types for believers' deliverance from sin/the world
Prophetic warnings against trusting Egypt (Isa 30–31, etc.) reinforce Egypt as false worldly power rather than a label for Jerusalem
The phrase 'spiritually is called' can be read as qualitative comparison rather than strict identification of the city's proper name
book_explanatory_advantages: Takes the locative clause 'where also our Lord was crucified' at face value to fix the referent as Jerusalem
Unifies Rev 11:8 with Gal 4:25 (Jerusalem in bondage), Isa 1:10 (Jerusalem addressed as Sodom), and Matt 23:37 / Rev 18:24 (prophet-killing) under one consistent city
Explains why the same city receives both spiritual names Sodom and Egypt in a single verse
Requires no non-literal re-reading of the crucifixion clause
counter_explanatory_advantages: Accounts for the large body of non-Revelation texts in which Egypt never means Jerusalem
Preserves the broad, stable Christian typology of Egypt as sin/world/bondage
Allows 'the great city' to remain Babylon/Rome or a generic world system in other Revelation passages
unresolved_objections: Whether every other occurrence of 'the great city' in Revelation must also be Jerusalem is left to the chapter and is outside the glossary entry
